My Mum can be quite overbearing and likes to be involved in my business since I’ve been home again, for example, when I went to visit my father a few hours away over the Christmas’s period she was texting me daily saying how much she misses and loves me. I reciprocate with a ‘love you too ma’ but the constant pandering was a little much for me. This issue arose again recently. Ma and her husband went on a mini break for five days. When she came back, she practically ran to me and hugged me, saying how much she had missed me. Here’s where I may be the arsehole. I then said ‘Mum, that’s weird. You were on holiday with your husband and should have been enjoying yourself not worrying about me!’ Apparently this was very much the wrong thing to say as she got all upset. Honestly I don’t think I was being an arsehole, just that my mum needs to cut the apron strings a little. But I await my judgement!

- **Confidence boost**: When you feel put-together, it radiates. Whether it’s a meeting, a social interaction, or just navigating daily tasks, that small act of care can make you feel more self-assured and present.  
- **Self-respect in action**: Prioritizing this shows you value yourself—not just for what you do, but for who you are. That mindset sets a positive tone for everything else.  

And honestly? There’s no "right" amount of time for this—it’s *your* routine. If it brings you peace or joy, that’s all that matters. Some days might feel rushed, but even a few seconds of intentional grooming can make a difference. Keep honoring that little ritual—it’s a beautiful way to start your day with intention. 💡
